rationale: No satisfying tensors exist under this template. The transformation rotates displacement vectors, requiring distances that these keys cannot encode. For example, demonstration 1 pixels (4,0) and (4,1) have identical nearest-colour keys but require outputs 8 and 7. The other key kinds also merge pixels requiring different outputs. These tensors are not a complete solution.

Pixel count reproduces all demonstrations: large-object counts 31, 14, 24, 16, and 30 map to 7, 3, 2, 3, and 2; marker counts 5 and 6 map to 0. Generalisation to unseen object sizes is not established.

No satisfying tensors exist under object_table. It only uniformly recolours existing components, whereas the outputs move interior colours to previously background exterior pixels. Changing the background cannot enable selective painting within a component. These tensors are not a solution.

No satisfying tensors exist under neighbor_table. In demonstration 2, pixels (3,2) and (6,6) have identical full 3x3 neighbourhoods but require outputs 8 and 0. Consequently every available neighbourhood key merges these pixels, regardless of background. These tensors are not a solution.

No satisfying tensors exist under neighbor_table. Demonstration 1 pixels (1,3) and (3,2) have identical full 3x3 neighbourhoods but require outputs 9 and 8. Every available key therefore merges them, regardless of background. These tensors are not a solution.

Enabling colour 8 fixes its missing rays, but no satisfying tensors exist under the stated semantics. Source-colour painting can produce only source colours; fixed painting uses one colour everywhere. Neither can preserve differently coloured rays while assigning colour 2 exclusively at intersections. These tensors are not a complete solution.
